bundles.name: Shape Semantics
bundles.description: What an output shape actually is: which elements leave, how each is transformed, which records are in scope, at what grain, and how two shapes compare and combine.
bundles.rationale: This is the only concern the registry entry assigns exclusively to this model - the shape data leaves in. Every other bundle either derives from it or references a model that owns its subject.

layers.name: Element Selection
layers.description: Which elements of a source structure may leave, expressed as sets over a declared default, and how those elements are addressed.

findings.name: Selection Sets and Default Treatment
findings.description: Include and exclude sets over source elements, the default treatment applied to everything the sets do not name, and whether the shape is closed against elements it has never seen.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Selection sets and their default are the policy record's own declarative content: structured values held with the policy, not a separate deliverable. Any file, table or document form is a projection of those values, so declaring an artifact here would confuse the shape with one of its encodings.

findings.name: Path Expression and Element Addressing
findings.description: How a shape addresses source elements across media, which grammar it uses, and what keeps an address resolvable when the source moves or repeats elements.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Addressing is reference data that only has meaning when resolved against the source schema owned by WM-DAT-004. Materialising it as a local artifact would duplicate a structure this model does not own and would go stale independently of the schema.

findings.name: Expansion, include, and hierarchical node selection
findings.description: Output shape is a graph, not only a column list. OData $expand includes related resources inline and may nest $select; context URLs describe projected+expanded entities. GraphQL selection sets are hierarchical down to scalars. FHIR _include/_revinclude add referenced resources; they cannot mix with _summary=text. JSON:API compound documents require full linkage except where sparse fieldsets exclude relationship fields. XACML Multiple Decision Profile interprets a multiple:content-selector XPath as one decision per node. This model records maximum expand depth, allowed navigation paths, and whether related resources inherit the parent policy or a nested policy.

layers.name: Element Treatment
layers.description: The transformation applied to a selected element before it leaves, its parameters, and whether it can be undone.

findings.name: Treatment Technique and Parameters
findings.description: The de-identification or shaping technique applied to an element, named from a governed vocabulary and parameterised well enough that the transformed value is reproducible.
findings.inline_only_rationale: A treatment declaration is structured content of the policy record and is meaningless apart from the element it qualifies. The transformation itself is executed by WM-XCT-038 over instance data this model never holds, so there is nothing local to materialise.

findings.name: Reversibility and Re-identification Coding
findings.description: Whether a treatment can be undone, by whom under which separate authority, and how a pseudonym or re-identification code namespace is referenced without this model holding a key.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Only the classification and the pointers live here. Keys, crosswalk tables and the authority to re-identify are held under WM-XCT-001 and WM-XCT-002; creating a local artifact would risk drawing sensitive reversal material into a policy record that is itself widely read.

layers.name: Record Scope and Grain
layers.description: Which records leave and at what level of summarisation, as distinct from which fields leave.

findings.name: Population and Record Scope
findings.description: The predicate deciding which records or instances appear in an output at all, and the disclosure created by membership in that set irrespective of field values.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The filter is a declarative clause of the policy record. Its evaluation happens in WM-XCT-038 and the floors it defers to are computed in WM-XCT-005, so a local artifact would either be empty or would restate values this model must not own.

findings.name: Aggregation Grain Declaration
findings.description: For summary-only shapes, the dimensions retained, the measures computed and the period, with cohort floors and privacy budgets referenced rather than defined.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The grain is a declarative clause. Computing thresholds, testing cohort sufficiency and accounting a privacy budget are all owned by WM-XCT-005, so any artifact produced here would reproduce that model's assurance output.

findings.name: Leaving-shape grain class
findings.description: A projection policy names exactly one primary grain for what may leave: (a) record-level subset — selected paths of authorised instances; (b) named summary — a predefined reduced view such as FHIR _summary=true/text/data; (c) aggregate-only — statistical functions over a grouping, with no microdata. ISO/IEC 20889 classifies aggregation and sampling as statistical de-identification tools; NIST SP 800-188 distinguishes publishing de-identified microdata, synthetic data, query interfaces, and protected enclaves. FHIR defines discrete summary modes including count-only.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Grain class is a closed vocabulary plus references to sibling models (XCT-005 for floors, DAT-004 for source). It is classification metadata, not a stored document.

layers.name: Shape Algebra
layers.description: The order relation on shapes and the operation that merges two applicable shapes into one no wider than either.

findings.name: Narrowing Order and Least-Disclosure Combination
findings.description: When one shape is no wider than another, how two applicable shapes combine into a single least-disclosure shape, and why this is distinct from deciding which policy takes precedence.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The algebra is a semantic rule set expressed once for the model, not per-instance content, and its execution belongs to callers. Recording it as an artifact would imply a deliverable that must be versioned separately from the model specification it defines.

bundles.name: Compiled Output Template
bundles.description: The concrete, verifiable shape a consumer actually receives, its derivation from pinned inputs, its encodings and the disclosure that survives beyond its stated values.
bundles.rationale: A shape only becomes checkable when compiled against a specific source schema and fingerprinted. This bundle exists so a served output can be verified and explained without re-reading the policy prose.

layers.name: Template Derivation
layers.description: How a template is produced from pinned inputs, identified, and kept aligned with a moving source schema.

findings.name: Compiled Template and Fingerprint
findings.description: The derived output shape a consumer receives, produced from one policy version against one source schema version and digested so any party can verify what was served.

findings.name: Source Schema Binding and Drift
findings.description: The dependency of a shape on a governed source schema version, how unresolved paths and newly appearing elements are detected, and who remediates.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Only the binding and its current resolution state are local; the schema itself and its validation contract are owned by WM-DAT-004. A local artifact would either copy that schema or become a second, competing source of truth about it.

layers.name: Disclosure Surface
layers.description: How the shape is rendered into concrete encodings, and what a recipient can still infer beyond the stated values.

findings.name: Encoding and Media Profile
findings.description: Which encodings a shape is approved to be served in, whether semantics are preserved in each, and which encoding choices are themselves disclosure decisions.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Encodings are projections of one semantic shape, so the model stays format-neutral by recording approvals and equivalence assertions rather than the encodings themselves. Concrete encoded forms are instances of the compiled template artifact already declared.

findings.name: Residual Disclosure and Side Channels
findings.description: What a recipient can still infer from a served output beyond its values: existence of a response, record counts, ordering, structural shape and the difference between error, refusal and empty result.
findings.inline_only_rationale: This is analytical content attached to the policy record. The runtime behaviour that realises uniform responses and padding is executed by WM-XCT-038, so declaring an artifact here would imply this model produces or holds the responses themselves.

bundles.name: Binding and Applicability
bundles.description: Where a shape applies: the targets and audiences it is attached to, the conditions under which it is the applicable shape, and the class and regime constraints that bound what is lawful.
bundles.rationale: A shape is reusable precisely because binding is separable from definition. This bundle keeps binding as pure reference so that authorization, party and classification semantics stay in their owning models.

layers.name: Binding Attachment
layers.description: The link record attaching a shape to a target and audience, and the declarative conditions for its applicability.

findings.name: Binding Target, Audience and Effective Window
findings.description: The attachment of one shape to a contract or grant, object type or audience class, with the window in which it is effective and the authority the binding presupposes.
findings.inline_only_rationale: A binding is a link record composed almost entirely of references. Materialising it would duplicate contract and party content owned by WM-XCT-002 and WM-XCT-001 and create a second place where an authorization appears to be recorded.

findings.name: Applicability Conditions
findings.description: The declarative conditions under which this shape is the applicable one, stated so an external evaluator can decide without this model performing or recording any decision.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Conditions are policy text carried with the shape. Attribute retrieval, evaluation, the resulting decision and its explanation all belong to WM-XCT-038, and producing an artifact here would look like a decision record this model must never own.

layers.name: Class and Regime Constraints
layers.description: Externally imposed lower bounds on treatment: governed sensitivity classes and legally prescribed shapes.

findings.name: Class-to-Treatment Minimum Matrix
findings.description: The governed table mapping an externally assigned sensitivity class to the weakest treatment a shape may apply, so that shapes can be checked mechanically rather than by reviewer opinion.

findings.name: Regime-Mandated and Regime-Forbidden Shapes
findings.description: Shapes that a legal or sectoral regime prescribes or forbids outright, recorded as named, cited constraints with their territorial and sectoral reach, never as restated law.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Regimes are cited, never copied. The model records pointers and reach so that legal text stays with its publisher and no compliance determination is made or implied here; an artifact would invite a local restatement of law that would silently go stale.

bundles.name: Assurance and Evidence
bundles.description: Why a shape is defensible: the identifiability role of each element, the assurance method claimed, and the effect of serving several shapes over the same population.
bundles.rationale: A shape without a stated basis cannot be reviewed or falsified. This bundle records the claim and its evidence pointer while leaving all quantification to the models that own it.

layers.name: Identifiability Declaration
layers.description: The role each element plays in re-identification and the basis on which the resulting shape is claimed adequate.

findings.name: Element Identifiability Roles
findings.description: Whether each selected element is a direct identifier, a quasi-identifier, a sensitive attribute or non-identifying, and the context assumptions behind that assignment.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Role assignment is analytical annotation on the shape, not a governed register: it neither replaces the sensitivity classification owned by WM-XCT-020 nor quantifies risk. Keeping it inline prevents it being mistaken for an authoritative classification record.

findings.name: Assurance Method and Evidence Pointer
findings.description: The basis on which the shape is claimed adequate - a rule-based method, an expert determination, or a formal privacy guarantee - held as a claim plus a pointer to evidence maintained elsewhere.
findings.inline_only_rationale: This model holds the claim and a pointer only. Risk quantification, cohort sufficiency and privacy budget accounting are owned by WM-XCT-005 and the adopting Dimension's assessment process, so producing an assurance artifact here would assert ownership of evidence this model does not generate.

layers.name: Cross-Release Effects
layers.description: Disclosure that arises from the set of shapes served rather than from any single shape.

findings.name: Release-Set Linkability
findings.description: The widening of disclosure when several shapes are served over the same population to the same or colluding recipients, through shared join keys, repeated queries or overlapping grains.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Linkability is a declared property of a set of shapes. Counting actual releases, maintaining a budget and enforcing a limit are runtime activities owned by WM-XCT-005 and WM-XCT-038, so no local artifact may hold a running total.

bundles.name: Interoperability and Publication
bundles.description: How the shape vocabulary maps onto external standards, how it behaves in holder-selected disclosure protocols, and the shape in which the policy record itself is published.
bundles.rationale: Shapes must travel between systems and must be browsable before any grant exists. This bundle records alignments and withheld conformance claims explicitly rather than assuming compatibility.

layers.name: Expression Alignment
layers.description: Mapping between local shape vocabulary and external policy-expression and disclosure standards, including what does not map.

findings.name: Policy Expression Crosswalk
findings.description: The mapping between this model's selection, treatment, scope and grain concepts and external policy-expression standards, recording mapping strength, unmapped concepts and conformance claims explicitly withheld.

findings.name: Selective Disclosure Protocol Fit
findings.description: How a governed shape behaves in protocols where the holder rather than the source chooses what is revealed, and where accountability for the final shape then sits.
findings.inline_only_rationale: This is an alignment statement about protocol behaviour, not a deliverable. Credential issuance, wallet holding and verification are separate subjects with their own models, and an artifact here would imply this model produces presentations.

layers.name: Publication and Catalogue
layers.description: The shape in which the policy record itself is disclosed to different readers.

findings.name: Self-Applied Policy Projection
findings.description: The projection under which the policy record itself leaves, since a disclosure policy is itself sensitive: a browsable summary, a template-only view for a bound recipient, and a full view for a reviewer.

bundles.name: Change and Fitness
bundles.description: Shape-specific consequences of change: whether a change widens or narrows disclosure, what must be emitted so a past disclosure stays explainable, and which signals mean a shape no longer protects adequately.
bundles.rationale: The generic policy lifecycle is owned elsewhere, but the question of whether a change lets more data out is purely a shape question and has no home in a generic policy model.

layers.name: Shape Change Semantics
layers.description: Classification of a change between two policy versions and the reproducibility obligations that follow.

findings.name: Disclosure Change Classification
findings.description: Whether a change between two policy versions narrows, widens or leaves disclosure unchanged, which dependents it affects, and what each class requires before taking effect.

findings.name: Served Output Reproducibility
findings.description: The minimum set of shape-identifying values that must accompany a served output so a past disclosure can be reconstructed and explained, and how long this model keeps them resolvable.
findings.inline_only_rationale: This finding defines an emission contract, not a record. The audit entry, its ordering, immutability, protection and retention are owned by WM-XCT-004, so declaring an artifact here would create a competing trail this model has no authority to hold.

layers.name: Fitness Signals
layers.description: Detectable conditions that mean a previously acceptable shape may now under-protect, with hand-off to the models that act.

findings.name: Shape Invalidation Signals
findings.description: The observable conditions that make a shape unfit - upward reclassification, schema drift, changed adversary context, expired assurance, regime change - recorded as signals with safe interim behaviour and an explicit hand-off, not as a state machine.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Signals and interim behaviour are declarative annotations on the shape. State transitions, approval and supersession are executed by WM-KNW-012 and any runtime response by WM-XCT-038, so an artifact here would be mistaken for a lifecycle record this model does not own.

model.name: Research Study
model.purpose: Represent one governed, versioned inquiry aggregate that pursues declared research questions or hypotheses through a protocol and design, defined populations, materials or phenomena, data collection, analysis and bounded findings.
model.scope_statement: Owns study identity and lineage, source-qualified classification, questions and hypotheses, protocol and design releases, study-scoped role, funding, site, ethics and privacy bindings, population and sampling assertions, cohorts, arms, interventions or exposures, conduct events, collection and analysis plans, result and finding assertions, registration and amendment history, output links, limitations, interoperability, access and retention. Research Project, Grant or Award, Experiment or Trial, Test Execution, Person, Participant, Population, Sample or Specimen, Site, Instrument, Observation, Measurement, Dataset, Software, Publication, Ethics Decision, Artifact and Audit masters remain external.
in_scope: Study identity, classification, questions, hypotheses, protocol, design, roles, funding and accountable authority
Ethics, privacy, population, eligibility, sampling, cohorts, sites, resources, interventions, exposures, conduct, observations and managed data
Analysis plans and executions, estimates, uncertainty, findings, limitations, registration, outputs, reproducibility, lifecycle, interoperability, access, retention and safe agents
out_of_scope: Independent project, grant, experiment, trial, test execution, person, participant, population, specimen, site, instrument, observation, dataset, software, publication, ethics-decision, artifact or audit master lifecycles
Inferring consent from participation, causality from association, truth from significance, generalizability from one sample, data fitness from completeness or reproducibility from one study
Implementing a laboratory, clinical-trial management system, electronic data capture system, statistical environment, repository, ethics board, registry or universal legal-compliance regime

boundary_notes.neighbor: Research Project, Programme, Grant or Award
boundary_notes.distinction: These organize objectives, funding, portfolios, schedules and delivery. A study is the inquiry aggregate with questions, protocol, evidence and findings and can be supported by several projects or awards.
These are contained or referenced conduct components with their own occurrence identity. The study owns broader design and synthesis but does not rewrite their evidence.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Participant, Population, Sample, Specimen, Site or Instrument
boundary_notes.distinction: The study owns scoped eligibility, selection, assignment and usage assertions. External masters retain identity, custody, lifecycle and source authority.
The study binds exact source and derived versions and records transformations and use. Observation and data-product masters retain their own semantics and provenance.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Finding, Scholarly Publication or other Output
boundary_notes.distinction: A study can issue bounded finding assertions and link released outputs. A publication is a separate authored and disseminated record and may contain claims not controlled by the study master.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Ethics Decision, Assessment or Audit Record
boundary_notes.distinction: Independent bodies and processes issue their own decisions and evidence. The study binds their exact versions and conditions without becoming the decision master.

functions.name: Register research study
functions.description: Create a stable study identity, classify its inquiry profile and resolve duplicates and neighboring aggregates.
preconditions: identity, duplicate, authority, profile and boundary checks pass
effects: one inquiry aggregate exists without copying its project, experiments, datasets or publications

functions.name: Release questions, design and protocol
functions.description: Freeze research questions, hypotheses, outcomes, methods and the protocol revision before governed conduct.
preconditions: scope, definitions, versions, outcomes, analysis intent and amendment rules validate
effects: intent remains distinguishable from later conduct and findings

functions.name: Authorize roles, ethics and privacy
functions.description: Bind accountable roles, oversight decisions, participant safeguards and privacy controls for the applicable profile.
preconditions: delegation, conflicts, approvals, conditions, consent requirements and access rules validate
effects: governed study activity can begin within explicit authority

functions.name: Define population, sample and assignment
functions.description: Pin target population, eligibility, sampling, size rationale, cohort or arm structure and assignment method.
preconditions: eligibility, unit, representativeness, power or precision and assignment checks pass
effects: inferential scope and selection limitations are inspectable

functions.name: Coordinate study conduct
functions.description: Record sites, resources, interventions or exposures and actual lifecycle and conduct events without rewriting the plan.
preconditions: resource, safety, timing, assignment, deviation and evidence rules validate
effects: planned and actual conduct remain attributable and comparable

functions.name: Capture observations and manage data
functions.description: Bind source observations and datasets to instruments, procedures, variables, transformations, quality and sharing plans.
preconditions: feature, property, value, unit, time, method, uncertainty, provenance, privacy and quality checks pass
effects: source evidence remains distinct from analysis and interpretation

functions.name: Execute analysis and assert results
functions.description: Run or record a pinned analysis and issue estimates and bounded result assertions.
preconditions: population, estimand, assumptions, versions, multiplicity, diagnostics, uncertainty and provenance validate
effects: results can be reviewed without treating significance as truth or association as causation

functions.name: Review and release findings and outputs
functions.description: Relate results to questions and release findings, datasets, software, materials or publications with limitations.
preconditions: evidence, interpretation, causal scope, generalizability, contradiction, rights, identifiers and access validate
effects: knowledge outputs remain connected to methods, evidence and study lineage

functions.name: Amend, correct, withdraw or supersede
functions.description: Preserve released history while appending protocol amendments, corrections, disputes, terminations, withdrawals or retractions.
preconditions: expected revision, impact, authority, affected scope and residual-validity checks pass
effects: later learning never silently erases prior intent, conduct, evidence or outputs

functions.name: Project, disclose, retain and audit
functions.description: Create version-pinned external views and perform controlled access, sharing and information-lifecycle operations.
outputs: projection, disclosure, disposition or audit event
preconditions: mapping loss, access, privacy, embargo, hold, tombstone, idempotency and post-checks validate
effects: research context remains interoperable, protected and accountable

composition.target: Research Project, Programme, Grant and Award models
composition.purpose: Resolve organizational sponsorship, portfolio, funding and delivery context while keeping inquiry identity separate.

composition.target: Experiment, Trial and Test Execution models
composition.purpose: Relate study-scoped conduct components without absorbing their occurrence identity, evidence or lifecycle.

composition.target: Participant, Population, Sample, Specimen, Site, Instrument and Resource models
composition.purpose: Bind study-scoped selection, assignment and use while preserving external identity, custody and authority.

composition.target: Observation, Measurement, Dataset, Software, Artifact and Audit models
composition.purpose: Link source and derived evidence with exact versions, transformations, integrity and provenance.

composition.target: Scholarly Publication and other Research Output models
composition.purpose: Link datasets, software, materials, protocols and publications as separately versioned outputs with access and correction history.

policies: A Research Study is not the supporting Research Project, one Experiment or Trial, a Dataset, a Publication, a Participant, a Specimen or an Analysis Procedure.

Protocol intent, actual conduct, raw observation, analysis execution, estimate, statistical evidence, interpretation, finding and policy or clinical conclusion remain separate source-qualified assertions.

Study ownership does not transfer ownership of project, grant, person, participant, population, site, specimen, instrument, observation, dataset, software, publication, ethics-decision, artifact or audit masters. Study disposition never cascades to linked masters.

Agents may validate, link and project allowlisted data, but participant contact, consent, intervention assignment, hazardous conduct, protected disclosure, scientific signoff and disposition require delegated authority and applicable policy controls.

coverage.claim: Codex fallback research covers a cross-disciplinary Research Study aggregate from protocol intent through evidence lineage, conduct, observations, data management, analyses, bounded findings, outputs, provenance and disposition. Entry kind (aggregate), source authority (16 primary tier-1 sources versioned and accessible), boundary distinctions (study vs. project, experiment, participant, observation, ethics), service-layer governance (access control, audit, retention, agent operation), and adversarial checks are defensible and source-grounded. Known gaps: composition relations held pending review, DataCite 4.7 reconciliation deferred, discipline and regional variants out of scope, single-provider mode lacks independent external review. No unresolved contradictions block reviewable-draft status.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Research Study aggregates protocol intent, evidence lineage and bounded findings under study-scoped authority; all external masters (project, participant, specimen, observation, dataset, publication, ethics, audit) deliberately retain independent identity and lifecycle authority. Consistent with Frascati (SRC-001), DDI Lifecycle (SRC-002, SRC-003), WHO TRDS (SRC-004), ClinicalTrials.gov (SRC-005), PROV (SRC-007) and DataCite (SRC-009, SRC-010). Frozen registry value 'standalone-mm' classifies record plane, not subject-model kind; aggregate is defensible schema choice.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root and Research Study entry kind
decisions.rationale: Research Study owns identity, lineage, protocol, design, conduct, evidence and findings as versioned inquiry aggregate; all external masters (project, participant, specimen, observation, dataset, publication, ethics, audit) remain deliberately external with independent lifecycle authority preserved. Boundary notes distinguish study from project (objectives and funding vs. inquiry and evidence), from experiment or trial (contained conduct vs. broader design), from participant or specimen (scoped eligibility vs. external master identity), from observation or dataset (study-scoped binding vs. data-product semantics), from publication (bounded findings vs. authored dissemination) and from ethics decision (study-scoped binding vs. independent oversight). Consistent with Frascati and clinical research governance standards (SRC-001, SRC-004, SRC-005).

decisions.concept: Source authority and version governance
decisions.rationale: All 16 sources declared primary authority_tier 1 with pinned versions, dates and accessible URLs. Governance includes Frascati 2015 (OECD standard for R&D classification), DDI Lifecycle 3.3 (data collection and maintainable structures), WHO TRDS 1.3.1 and ClinicalTrials.gov current (protocol registration), OGC OMS and ISO 19156:2023 (observation and measurement), W3C PROV, DCAT 3, RFC 3339 (provenance, discovery, timestamps), DataCite 4.6/4.7 (metadata and output identification), NIH DMS Policy (data sharing), NIH Privacy Best Practices (de-identification), NIST Privacy Framework (privacy governance), 45 CFR Part 46 (human subjects protection), UK National Archives (retention and disposal). DataCite 4.6/4.7 reconciliation already explicitly flagged in known_omissions; defer delta review to relation-approval phase. All source references remain live and verifiable.

decisions.concept: Composition relations and external master autonomy
decisions.rationale: No approved relation rows were supplied. Parent and reference relations to external masters, including research project, grant or award, experiment, trial, test execution, person, participant, population, sample, specimen, site, resource, instrument, observation, measurement, dataset, software, publication, ethics decision, artifact and audit record, are explicitly held as composition gaps pending relation definitions and approval. Service policies declare that study ownership does not transfer to linked masters and study disposition never cascades to linked masters. This is appropriate for a reviewable draft and preserves independent master identity, authority and lifecycle. Composition completeness cannot be claimed until relations are bound and reviewed.

decisions.concept: Service-layer governance and access control
decisions.rationale: Service layers properly separate study master from implementation systems and enforcement. Access default rule denies direct participant identifiers, sensitive attributes, consent records, confidential sponsor material, protected locations, unpublished hypotheses, embargoed outputs and raw evidence unless purpose-bound Dimension policy permits minimum necessary view. Roles and responsibilities explicitly distributed (sponsor, principal investigator, protocol steward, ethics body, data steward, reviewer, privacy and records steward). CRUD operations distinguish create (bind study and pre-conduct governance), update (append lifecycle, conduct, observation, analysis and finding events), delete (apply ethics, retention, participant-rights and legal-hold policy). Agent bootstrap, idempotency, preconditions, dry-run and post-check requirements are explicit. This governance framework is sound and consistent with research integrity, participant protection and records-management standards (SRC-005, SRC-011, SRC-012, SRC-013, SRC-014, SRC-015).

decisions.concept: Adversarial checks and research-integrity safeguards
decisions.rationale: Five adversarial checks defend against critical failures. First, reject a study without stable identity, explicit questions or purpose, pinned protocol and design, accountable authority and evidence lineage. Second, reject consent inferred from enrolment, hypothesis support from significance, causality from association, generalizability from sample size or reproducibility from one study. Third, reject an amendment or correction that overwrites released questions, eligibility, sampling, outcomes, conduct, observations, analyses, findings or publications. Fourth, reject copied participant, specimen, observation, dataset, publication, ethics or project masters whose independent identity and lifecycle are lost. Fifth, reject agent contact, intervention assignment, protected disclosure, scientific signoff or disposition outside delegated authority and applicable policy controls. These checks are source-grounded in SRC-001, SRC-005, SRC-007, SRC-013 and SRC-014 and remain non-negotiable.

decisions.concept: Regional and disciplinary scope boundaries
decisions.rationale: Model is cross-disciplinary kernel anchored on clinical and statistical R&D sources (OECD Frascati, DDI, WHO, ClinicalTrials.gov, NIST). Service-layer documentation explicitly notes: Human-subject, animal, environmental, export-control, privacy, intellectual-property, clinical, research-integrity and records obligations vary by jurisdiction, institution and discipline. OECD Frascati supplies statistical R&D boundary, not universal operational lifecycle. DDI strongest for social, behavioural, economic data; WHO and ClinicalTrials.gov are clinical-trial profiles; OMS observation-oriented; DCAT and DataCite focus discovery. 45 CFR Part 46 applies within US regulatory context only. Discipline-specific profiles (behavioral sciences, environmental sciences, biomedical research, social research, engineering, computer science) and regional variants (non-OECD contexts, non-US regulatory frameworks) must define their own ethics, privacy, consent, retention and disclosure policies before canonical deployment. Do not claim universal applicability.

publicationHolds: Codex single-provider fallback research: Claude Sonnet and Grok 4.6 each timed out on their one bounded 120-second attempt for WM-ACT-036. No external provider result was admitted. The source-grounded Codex fallback passed local schema validation and the required separate no-tools adversarial audit. The result remains reviewable-draft without an independent second-provider evidence pass, and this hold must remain visible.

Live source and version verification required: The 16 declared official sources must be verified against their live resources at canonical promotion. The property-level DataCite crosswalk is pinned to version 4.6 while the official release history lists version 4.7 as current from 3 March 2026. A 4.6 to 4.7 delta review and round-trip tests are required before canonical interoperability claims.

Composition relations held pending review: No approved relation rows were supplied. Candidate parent, composition, reference and output relations to external masters remain proposed only. Typed relation definitions, ownership, lifecycle linkage and no-cascade behavior must be reviewed before claiming composition completeness; this does not block publication of the internally valid reviewable draft.

Discipline-specific and regional profiling deferred: Model anchors on clinical and statistical R&D sources (Frascati, DDI, WHO, ClinicalTrials.gov, NIST). Discipline-specific profiles for behavioral sciences, environmental sciences, biomedical research, social research, engineering and computer science require separate ethics, privacy, consent and retention bindings. 45 CFR Part 46 applies within US regulatory context only; international, European, non-OECD and non-English-speaking contexts require regionalized governance policies. These variants are out of scope. Cannot claim universal applicability or cross-jurisdictional compliance.

Single-provider mode and absence of external review: Codex is the sole admitted research provider after the bounded Claude and Grok attempts timed out. The no-tools adjudication is a separate audit, not an independent evidence pass. The result must remain reviewable-draft until an independent external review is available, and the current waiver must stay visible in publication notices.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Relation definitions and composition mappings: Explicit typed relations to external masters must be formalized with identity strategy, ownership, lifecycle linkage rules and no-cascade semantics. Candidate registry and composition rows remain unapproved and need steward review.

DataCite 4.6/4.7 interoperability reconciliation: The property-level mapping is pinned to DataCite Metadata Schema 4.6 while the official release history lists version 4.7 as current from 3 March 2026. Reconcile property and cardinality deltas, map relevant changes, verify round-trip fidelity and test the crosswalk with real registry records before canonical promotion.

Discipline-specific and regional profile variants: Clinical research (ClinicalTrials.gov, WHO TRDS, FDA IND/IDE), statistical R&D (Frascati), behavioral sciences, environmental sciences, biomedical research, social research, engineering and computer science each require discipline-specific protocol, ethics, privacy, consent and retention profiles. US regulatory context (45 CFR Part 46, FDA, HIPAA, NIH DMS) must be separated from European (GDPR, EMA, national ethics boards), international (World Bank, UNICEF), non-OECD and non-English-speaking contexts. Governance policies must be regionalized and require local ethics and legal review.

Agent operation policies and implementations: AGENTS.md bootstrap structure is defined (Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL, Processes URL) but no concrete agent implementations, delegation authorities, idempotency keys, preconditions, dry-run mode, expected-revision assertions or post-condition verifications are supplied. Separate agent-operation specification required before access, sharing, retention and disposition operations can be delegated to agents. Audit trail and tamper-evidence requirements must be explicit.

Bidirectional relation verification and master-side study discovery: No reverse mappings provided from external masters (project, experiment, participant, dataset, publication, ethics decision) back to study aggregate. Must verify that study identity is resolvable from external master references and that bidirectional links preserve both study and master autonomy. Cross-system consistency checks and conflict-resolution rules for competing assertions must be defined.
